**ICSG/STAT36/5 ICSG/EEC29/6** 

**International Copper Study Group Joint ICSG Statistical Committee and Environmental and Economic Committee Meeting 28**<sup>**th**</sup> **September 2010, 9.00am – 12.30pm Antofagasta, Chile** 

# **Joint ICSG Statistical Committee and Environmental and Economic Committee Report** 

## **1. Opening of the Meeting by the Chairmen** 

The meeting was opened by the Chairman of the Statistical Committee, Mr Daniel Edelstein (United States). 

## **2. Adoption of the Agenda** 

(Background Document ICSG/STAT36/1 (Rev.1) and ICSG/EEC29/1 (Rev.1)) 

The revised agenda was adopted as tabled. 

## **3. Introduction to the International Copper Study Group by the Secretary-General** 

ICSG Secretary-General Mr Don Smale presented an introduction to the International Copper Study Group, including information about the ICSG membership, mandate, objectives and functions, publications and meetings. 

## **4. Global 2010/2011 Copper Market Supply and Demand Forecasts and Longer Term Production Capacity Developments** 

(Background Document ICSG/STAT36/2) 

ICSG Chief Statistician Ms Ana Rebelo presented the results of the Preliminary Forecast, including information about ICSG data sources, the main global assumptions regarding refined copper usage and copper production behind the forecast, and expected changes in production and usage by region. In 2010, world mine production is expected to increase by 2% to 16.2 million metric tons, while refined production and usage are both expected to increase by around 4% this year, resulting in a market surplus of 200 thousand metric tons (kt). For 2011, increased usage is expected to outstrip the forecast increase in refined copper production, resulting in a production-usage deficit of around 435 kt. The presentation also included an overview of the development of copper mines and plants, including longer term production capacity developments by country, region and plant type until 2014. The industry advisor from Anglo American suggested that the figure for the disruption allowance for mine production also be included. A draft statistical press release was distributed and participants were invited to provide comments or suggestions to the Chief Statistician prior to its release. 

## **5. Presentations on Developments in Key Regions** 

The Chairman invited Mr Mark Loveitt from the International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC), to deliver his presentation on Europe. After describing the organization and purpose of the IWCC, the presentation covered recent trends in demand for copper in Europe, specifically demand for copper semis, with recent data provided in part by ICA and CRU. Following the dramatic 

decrease in semis demand in Europe in 2009, when demand for rolled products and brass rod were off 25% and 30%, respectively, year-on-year, it was noted that demand in Europe was recovering in 2010, although in some instances demand had yet to return to pre-2009 levels as semis production a

nd demand had been migrating to Asia in recent years. 

The Chairman then invited Mr Juan Carlos Guajardo of CESCO to deliver his presentation on Latin America. The presentation was focused on supply, covering copper production and investment in Latin America and especially copper mine production in the key producing countries such as Chile. Main topics included the large amount of investment in mining in Latin America in recent years (over $200 billion invested in the last decade), and the large on-going investments, including the large number of exploration sites in Chile with projected exploration and development budgets of greater than $1.5 billion. The presentation also covered the challenges to bringing new supply on-stream, including the sharp increases in mine production costs, which have doubled in just the last four year period. 

Mr Natsumi Kamiya of JOGMEC was then invited to deliver his presentation on supply and demand for copper in Japan. The presentation covered recent trends in refined copper production, sales and exports in Japan, as well as the changing sources of refined copper supply, a breakdown of Japanese copper cable and brass sales, and major overseas base metal mining investment by Japanese companies. In addition, information about the mineral resources policy of Japan and the role of JOGMEC was presented, including information about JOGMEC’s Joint Venture Exploration Scheme. 

ICSG Economist Mr Joseph Pickard delivered his presentation on key copper market developments in China. Among the topics covered were: meeting demand in China; sources of copper; recent trends in refined copper usage; the changing structure of the Chinese semis fabricating industry and the role of scrap; China’s demand for copper with respect to the rest of the world; and future trends for Chinese production and usage, including the most recent ICSG forecasts for China. The industry advisor from BHP Billiton suggested that the secretariat could use its improved data on China, including improved scrap data, to approximate a figure closer to real refined usage in China as compared to the apparent usage calculation currently employed by ICSG. 

Mr Dan Edelstein, Chairman of the Statistical Committee and representative from the US Geological Survey, then delivered his presentation on the United States. Among the topics covered included the history of copper supply and demand in the United States and the decreasing demand for refined copper and falling semis production there as capacity migrated to Mexico and Asia. He noted that despite reduced usage and the potential for increased mine output, the United States is likely to remain significantly import dependant for refined copper owing to the loss of its significant secondary smelting capacity and to reduced primary and secondary smelting/refining capacity. In addition, information was presented on the limited role of government in recent years in promoting the copper industry in the United States.

## **6. Investment as a new but readily understood market force in copper** 

Mr Peter Hollands, Managing Director, Bloomsbury Minerals Economics, delivered his presentation on investment buying as an aspect of demand, followed by discussion. Among the topics covered included the changing relationship between prices and stocks, the need to incorporate twin market balances (in the physical market and the futures market) in copper market analysis, counter-arguments and alternative interpretations of the changing price and market balance relationship, and finally information about price forecasting based on the twinbalance approach. Several questions were raised, including how BME estimates hedged short positions and whether their analysis pertains to markets in either contango or backwardation. 

## **7. Threats to Current Applications and Evolution of New Applications** 

Mr Miguel Riquelme, Regional Director for the International Copper Association in Latin America, delivered his presentation on threats to current applications and the evolution of new copper applications. Among the topics covered included recent gains and losses from substitution, substitution by region and product, the major drivers of substitution including cost level and cost volatility, the major substitute materials and the potential for reversibility by market segment. Information on new copper applications was also provided, including products relating to heat exchange, marine aquaculture, automotive and data communication, antimicrobial surfaces, seismic energy dissipation and renewable energy. 

## **8. Copper Scrap Market Issues and Developments in the Semi-Fabricators Industry** 

(Background Document ICSG/EEC29/2) 

ICSG Head of Economics and Environment Mr Carlos Risopatron delivered his presentation on scrap market issues and developments in the semi-fabricators industry. Topics covered included: ICSG Research on Copper and Copper Alloy Scrap Markets; the 2010 Copper and Copper Alloys Fabrication Directory; and Fabrication and Use of Copper and Copper Alloy Products. In addition, actions for member countries included: 1) approval of the final report of the China semis capacity update completed in recent months and approval for publication and sale; 2) reallocation of 5,000 Euros from Unallocated Project Funds to complete funding the 70 Plants Survey of Refined, Scrap and Alloy Copper Use in China, to be co-funded by ICSG, ILZSG and INSG; 3) approval of the sale of the  Global Copper Recyclables Survey and the Regulatory Developments Report; and 4) new proposals from member countries on ICSG copper scrap and copper fabrication data collection and research. There were no objections to these proposals in either the Joint Statistical Committee and Environmental and Economic Committee Meeting or the Standing Committee meeting held later that day. 

## **9. Other Business** 

No other business items were introduced. The Chairman of the Statistical Committee recognized th

e significant contribution that Joe Pickard had made to the ICSG, and wished him well in his new position. 

## **10. Arrangements for the Chairmen’s Report** 

The Chairman advised that a report would be prepared and distributed and then adjourned the meeting.
